text:
lia: FYI — Acme reports that after yesterday's model bump to rwd-1.5 their assistant answers became noticeably more abrupt and omitted context. They say it used to give 2-3 sentence explanations and now it's 1 short line. They've attached repro examples.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout of rwd-1.5 -> hosted API completed at 1778898000 (canary 10%).

matt: thanks lia. can you paste a minimal repro (prompt + response before/after) and one request id? also is this only a particular prompt family or across the board?

lia: short repro below. customer provided explicit before/after with same prompt and same control params (temperature, top_p). request id: req_0a9f3c.
```
# prompt
User: "Explain how to reset a password for our web portal."

# rwd-1.4 (pre-bump)
Assistant: "To reset a password, go to Settings > Account > Reset Password. Click 'Reset', check your email for a link, and follow the steps. If you don't see the email, check spam or contact support with your account id."

# rwd-1.5 (post-bump)
Assistant: "Go to Settings > Account > Reset Password. Click 'Reset' and follow the emailed link."
```
lia: customer also included token stats from their side: pre ~220 tokens, post ~78 tokens for same prompt+completion. they flagged this because the trimmed answer removed helpful troubleshooting hints.

priya: quick clarifying q: were decoding defaults changed in the serving layer for rwd-1.5? max_tokens / stop sequences / streaming behaviour?

lia: customer claims they passed identical params in their client. snippet they sent: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-infer","model_version":"rwd-1.5","prompt":"...","temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.95}'
```
response truncated example above; request id mapped to our logs: 1778901190 -> req_0a9f3c.

matt: i'm pulling the server-side logs now. looks like the model name mapping layer translates `rwd-infer` + version tag to serving config. will check if a default max_new_tokens or stopping token was changed. also will run the same prompt against a pinned rwd-1.4 locally.

priya: looking at rollout config: the rwd-1.5 service profile includes a change we made to reduce average token output for cost reasons — default `max_new_tokens` was set to 40 at the routing layer for the hosted default. that would explain shorter completions even if clients didn't set max_tokens.

jamie: oof. was that change surfaced in release notes/console? if not, we need to notify customers and consider rollback for affected customers.

matt: confirmed local run against rwd-1.4 reproduces longer answer. rwd-1.5 with routing-layer `max_new_tokens=40` reproduces the shorter answer.

lia: Acme is sensitive to tone/verbosity for their UX. i just routed their customer_id (acme-42) back to rwd-1.4 at 1778901200 and asked them to verify. they just pinged: tone restored.

priya: i'll open a quick rollback PR to restore previous default in the routing profile and add an explicit note in the release changelog about the default token cap.

jamie: also propose a canary metric for "answer-length delta" vs baseline for future rollouts (small evaluation set of prompts measuring median token output and a semantic-sufficiency check). can product/ML pair on this?

matt: happy to help — we can add an automated eval job that runs the canonical prompt set and flags >15% median token shift.

lia: customer confirmed: "Thanks, tone looks back to normal." they want a root-cause update and a timeline. I'll open an incident ticket with the sample prompts + our findings. :thumbsup:

jamie: thanks everyone. assign action items: priya -> rollback PR + changelog (P0), matt -> eval job proposal (P1), lia -> incident ticket + customer update (P0).
